cli.name: kae dru-check --board
cli.note: run the KiCad pass on this .kicad_pcb (its layer names and project file count; slower: a full DRC per probe)

cli.name: kae dru-check --kicad
cli.note: also run KiCad's own parser (auto: when kicad-cli is found)

cli.name: kae dru-check --strict
cli.note: treat warnings as errors

cli.name: kae dru-check --vocab
cli.note: KiCad vocabulary label for the static pass (default: the installed KiCad's, else the newest bundled release)

cli.name: kae place --angles
cli.note: let parts turn to any multiple of STEP degrees, not only right angles (heatsink-mount packages keep right angles; CP-SAT stays on right angles)

cli.name: kae place --anneal-args
cli.note: JSON of annealer weights for experiments, e.g. '{"w_phys": 2.0}' (w_phys, w_wl, w_cong, w_order, w_disp, cong_args, ...)

cli.name: kae place --drc
cli.note: KiCad DRC on the result, fed back until clean (auto: when kicad-cli is found)

cli.name: kae place --drc-rounds
cli.note: repair rounds driven by KiCad's DRC

cli.name: kae place --edge-mate
cli.note: place staged footprints that carry Edge.Cuts where their open pieces close the outline exactly (default: hold them and flag outline_incomplete)

cli.name: kae place --fix
cli.note: keep these parts at their input pose (fixed obstacles, as locked parts)

cli.name: kae place --fix-class
cli.note: keep every part of these classes at its input pose: connectors, mounting, user (kae.place.fixed.classify)

cli.name: kae place --no-anneal
cli.note: seed and legalize only (= --stages seed,legalize)

cli.name: kae place --no-physics
cli.note: routability and legality only (ablation)

cli.name: kae place --probe-jitter
cli.note: with --probe-select: candidates after the first start from a seed stage moved by F x the board span (0: annealer seeds only)

cli.name: kae place --probe-parallel
cli.note: with --probe-select: probe P candidates at once (each probe runs Freerouting)

cli.name: kae place --probe-select
cli.note: place N times (seeds seed..seed+N-1) and keep the placement a quick kae.route probe leaves the fewest open connections on (physics within 10%%; off by default)

cli.name: kae place --recheck
cli.note: independent KiCad DRC of the output with the safety checks forced on; findings go to the report's hazards (auto: when kicad-cli is found and time is left)

cli.name: kae place --relax-bodies
cli.note: parts without a courtyard: 'off' (default) keeps their bodies as obstacles; 'escalate' frees them to their pads when legalization fails; 'auto' also up front on

cli.name: kae place --report
cli.note: also write the JSON report here

cli.name: kae place --severity
cli.note: placement legality: courtyards, copper-to-edge, rule areas, clearance, shorts and hole clearance are errors whatever the project says. 'strict_then_level_c' (de

cli.name: kae place --stages
cli.note: stages to run; seed and legalize always run, so 'seed,legalize' skips the annealer

cli.name: kae place --time
cli.note: wall-clock seconds the caller allows

cli.name: kae place --workers
cli.note: CP-SAT threads (default: KAE_WORKERS or cores/2)

cli.name: kae.joint.cli run --keep
cli.note: keep the work directory

cli.name: kae.joint.cli run --max-iters
cli.note: repair iterations at most (default: as many as the time allows; 0: staged pipeline only)

cli.name: kae.joint.cli run --no-finish
cli.note: no finishing stage (the full bridge over the whole board in a reserved share of the time)

cli.name: kae.joint.cli run --no-modules
cli.note: no module stage (kae place, then the bridge)

cli.name: kae.joint.cli run --no-physics
cli.note: placer without physics terms (ablation)

cli.name: kae.joint.cli run --physics-fidelity
cli.note: routed-loop physics: fast closed forms (default), exact PEEC everywhere, or multi (closed forms to search, PEEC on each decision's fast top K and on finished bo

cli.name: kae.joint.cli run --physics-k
cli.note: top K that multi re-scores by PEEC (default 4)

cli.name: kae.joint.cli run --recheck
cli.note: independent KiCad DRC of the output with the safety checks forced on; findings go to the report's hazards (auto: when kicad-cli is found and time is left)

cli.name: kae.joint.cli run --route-parallel
cli.note: P > 1: the finishing stage is kae.route.portfolio with P parallel restarts (critical_cli --last-mile-soft, then the bridge), and a window left open gets 2 more

cli.name: kae.joint.cli run --set
cli.note: loop or stage option, JSON values (loop.DEFAULTS, stages.STAGE_KEYS, kae.route.constraints.DEFAULTS, bridge.KEY; unknown keys are an error). margin is the loop'

cli.name: kae.joint.cli run --start
cli.note: a placed board to start from instead of running the placer

cli.name: kae.joint.cli run --time
cli.note: wall seconds for everything

cli.name: kae.route.cli finish --drc-s
cli.note: seconds one DRC of BOARD takes (for the estimates)

cli.name: kae.route.cli finish --input-drc
cli.note: KiCad DRC JSON of BOARD with INPUT's rules (the gate reuses it)

cli.name: kae.route.cli finish --parts
cli.note: comma list of tails, taut, power, trim

cli.name: kae.route.cli finish --recheck
cli.note: independent KiCad DRC of the output with the safety checks forced on; findings go to the report's hazards (auto: when kicad-cli is found and time is left)

cli.name: kae.route.cli lastmile --recheck
cli.note: independent KiCad DRC of the output with the safety checks forced on; findings go to the report's hazards (auto: when kicad-cli is found and time is left)

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --fanout
cli.note: enable Freerouting's fanout pre-pass (narrows tracks)

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --fanout-first
cli.note: fanout for the first route only; repair rounds re-route without it

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --keep
cli.note: keep the temporary work directory

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --no-blocked
cli.note: at the end, diagnose the connections still open: the report's "blocked" names the board rule (or kae default) that makes each impossible (kae.route.blocked)

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --no-finish
cli.note: at the end, when time is left: the finish stage (rule D tails, taut arcs, power copper, one journaled DRC gate; kae.route.finish)

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --no-last-mile
cli.note: after the repair rounds, join what is still open with the grid router (kae.route.lastmile; default on, --no-last-mile turns it off)

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --no-neckdown
cli.note: Freerouting's neck-down at pins, floored at the board's legal minimum width

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --no-thermal
cli.note: no thermal-spoke corridors in the repair loop

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --pad-shapes
cli.note: pin polygons in the DSN: KiCad's (arc chords inside the pad) or ones that contain the pad

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --planes
cli.note: inner plane layers: traces there cost plane_cost x (cost), none (strict), none unless a repair round has open connections (keep), or KiCad's layer types (allow)

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --recheck
cli.note: independent KiCad DRC of the output with the safety checks forced on; findings go to the report's hazards (auto: when kicad-cli is found and time is left)

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --rounds
cli.note: repair rounds at most, or 'auto' (until two rounds in a row are not better, or the time)

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --router-share
cli.note: share of the budget for the first routing, or 'auto' (0.6 up to 1,500 s, then all but 600 s: the router stops by itself and the repair rounds get the rest)

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --seed
cli.note: 0: KiCad's item order; others: a permuted order

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --set
cli.note: override one of kae's own defaults (e.g. ignored_clearance_floor=0.08); a KAE_<KEY> text variable in the KiCad project overrides this in turn

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --thermal-all
cli.note: spoke corridors for every thermal pad up front

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --time
cli.note: total budget in seconds

cli.name: kae.route.cli route --workdir
cli.note: keep intermediate files here (DSN, SES, DRC reports)

cli.name: restart.py --alt
cli.note: completion-first: the command of the second run on a clean board

cli.name: restart.py --check-placement
cli.note: methods that place: unlocked parts outside the outline, or parts on top of each other (courtyards, pad-to-pad shorts) beyond the input's, make an attempt illega

cli.name: restart.py --final
cli.note: command for one last pass on the kept board (@IN@, @BEST@, @OUT@, @SEED@, @TIME@), its time reserved from the start; kept only when KiCad ranks it better

cli.name: restart.py --final-s
cli.note: seconds for the final pass; 0 = FINAL_MIN_S plus one DRC of the board

cli.name: restart.py --finish
cli.note: command for the finish stage on the kept board after --final (@IN@, @BEST@, @OUT@, @SEED@, @TIME@, @DRC@: the judge's DRC report of @BEST@, @DRC_S@: one judgeme

cli.name: restart.py --finish-s
cli.note: seconds for the finish pass; 0 = an estimate from the input's pad count plus two DRCs

cli.name: restart.py --max-attempts
cli.note: stop launching after this many (deterministic methods: 1); 0 = no limit

cli.name: restart.py --open-alt
cli.note: completion-first: the command of the second run when phase 1's board is not clean, on that board (@BEST@), instead of COMMAND again; kept when it ranks no worse

cli.name: restart.py --open-rest
cli.note: completion-first with --open-alt: the --open-alt run's unused budget goes to one more run (COMMAND with the next seed, or --alt on a clean board with --open-res

cli.name: restart.py --open-rest-alt
cli.note: with --open-rest: when the kept board is clean, that run is --alt (kept when no worse)

cli.name: restart.py --policy
cli.note: completion-first: two runs of this wrapper in --time (half each). The second is --alt (e.g. the module stage) when the first run's board is clean, else another

cli.name: restart.py --resume
cli.note: share of each wave after the first that continues from the best board so far (@BEST@, KAE_RESUME=1); 0 = every attempt starts from the input

cli.name: restart.py --scale-first
cli.note: first-s x sqrt(footprints / 40) when above 1: big boards need longer single attempts

cli.name: restart.py --screen
cli.note: methods that place: successive halving over placements instead of the fixed waves (fresh attempts at --screen-s, the best of each rung resumed with eta x the bu

cli.name: restart.py --screen-s
cli.note: rung-0 budget (0: first-s; kae staged at half of it overran its budget: placing alone takes 60-100 s)

cli.name: restart.py --slack
cli.note: an attempt may run budget x slack before it is killed (methods whose budget is solver CPU time and that spend more on KiCad I/O around it)

cli.name: restart.py --time
cli.note: wall seconds for everything
